summary.name: 2D Rigged Animation: a supplemental design reference in the Animation Techniques category, not a directly named style in the source collection.
summary.visualIdentity: Character artwork is split into rigged parts with defined joints, pivots, occlusion, motion limits, and replaceable expressions. Poses move through arcs, anticipation, and settling, with replacement poses drawn when needed. Avoid excess stretch, exposed joint seams, and claims that every frame was redrawn.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to illustrated mascots, anime, cartoon, storybook, and rigged character scenes, or product and explainer scenes with an existing expressive character. Use it alone when poses, arcs, and expressions carry the story. Inferred: it suits character-hosted explainers and onboarding stories.
summary.limitations: Requires rigged or layered character assets; adapt or omit when artwork lacks readable eyes, suitable layers, or a rig. Do not alter actual footage without an appropriate production method. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.
summary.palette: Example only, for new artwork without an approved palette; approved character palettes override it. Suggested discrete tokens: background #F4EDDF, foreground #2C4249, accent_1 #7A9A91, accent_2 #C7876F, with gradients disabled. Background and foreground are layout roles, not recoloring instructions. Foreground on background measures 9.092, passing the 4.5 normal-text target. Accent-to-foreground pairs (3.459, 3.593) fail, so accents stay decorative. Two-color checks miss images, textures, video, and animated lighting, so recheck composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Use parent-child transforms, pivots, and layer order to sequence part movement. Smooth authored easing suits most actions, but cuts, impacts, and reading holds need not ease. Video state derives from seekable composition time. Optional references, none mandatory: motion-006 gives bounded pupil following with optional delayed brows, head tilt, and blinks, requiring eye layers and not representing viewer tracking; motion-012 and motion-015 provide progress-driven chapter handoffs and narrative stages. Pointer and scroll input apply only to interactive delivery.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified in the source, and no fixed music, voice, or effect layer is required. Task-specific options include topic-matched restrained music or ambience, voiceover, sparse sound accents on key actions, or silence during reading holds. Honor explicit user audio first and never invent assets. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping, and verify picture sync.
summary.assetRequirements: Prepare layered character assets with alpha transparency, consistent dimensions, and clear naming, or numbered frames with a layer manifest; inspect them before composition. The rig needs joints, pivots, occlusion layers, replaceable expressions, and eye layers for gaze. Keep source artwork and approved colors unchanged, and load fonts and assets before rendering. Specific asset lists are unspecified.
summary.combinations: Use alone for character-led scenes. Add hybrids only when the character must explain a system or inhabit an environment, keeping the rig and palette dominant. Suggested style-109 diagram support uses foreground-token strokes, accents only on the active path, and no lines crossing joints or face. Suggested style-101 parallax backgrounds keep the character on one depth layer, use lower-contrast tints, overscan edges, and never occlude the face.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames handles composition, timing, sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation is recorded; an existing React project alone is insufficient. SVG renders shapes, masks, and strokes; PixiJS is optional for many sprites with fixed-time updates; Rough.js is optional for sketch-style marks only. GSAP drives a paused, seekable timeline; Motion is optional and must be synchronized explicitly. chroma.js validates colors and contrast. Verify key frames and the decoded video.
